texts.facts: 4. By this petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has prayed for the following reliefs:- "26. 5. The brief facts of the case are as under:- 5.1. The petitioner is a public trust registered under the provisions of the Bombay Public Trust Act, 1950. On 15.05.2017, the respondent No.2 - Gujarat Building and other Construction Workers Welfare Board issued an advertisement inviting the tenders for empanelment of the agencies for imparting safety and health training to its registered construction workers. The petitioner - Trust, being eligible, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined applied for allotment of the tender. The respondent No.2, considering the past experience of the petitioner for imparting safety and health training to the registered construction workers, informed the petitioner by letter dated 29.07.2017 that its tender had been accepted. Thereafter, the work order dated 07.05.2018 was issued to the petitioner for imparting training at Bhavnagar and Navsari districts and the petitioner was required to conduct 70 training classes in both the districts. The work order stipulated the following terms and conditions:- "(1) The agency will be required to start training classes in the specified district and shall inform in writing to the District Project Manager of the concerned district as well as the State Project Officer of the Head Office before starting the training. (2) The Agency shall be required to give training to the construction workers registered in trades prescribed by this office. (3) The agency shall provide training to the al construction workers the construction site/where the workers are settled, as per the instructions of the Board's office. (4) The Agency has to provide theory for 03 hours and practical training for 02 hours in the training class per day at site and, its documentation shall require to be produced before the District office. (5) The Agency shall have to maintain the original attendance sheet in regard to the presence of the Trainees and, on completion of training, the same shall require to be produced in the Board's office. (6) The photographs of the trainees during the training shall be required to be produced. (9) As decided vide Resolution dated 21/05/2015 of the Labor and Employment Department, the cost will be incurred within the limit of Rs.500 per trainee out of which, the amount of Rs. 186/- per trainee for each 5 hours shall be paid and, the beneficiaries shall be paid Rs.50/-towards food. Whereas, the Agency shall be paid Rs.264/- per beneficiary for taking and bringing the trainees within the limitation of the aforesaid cost. (10) The amount of stipend to the trainees shall be paid by board through DBT. Therefore, the agency may note to send the list of beneficiaries in Excel format (as per attached statement) through email as well as in hard copy. (11) The agency will also have to arrange a video calling facility at the spot. (12) If the training Agency shall violate any of the aforesaid terms, if postpones the Training program or the Agency becomes insolvent then under such circumstances, the Board shall have the powers to cancel the training. Agency cannot claim payment of arrears. (13) If it appears that the training Agency has failed to fulfill the prescribed obligation, the Member Secretary may stop the training." 5.2. Further, the Project Manager of the respondent No.2 issued work completion certificate on completion of each training programme, certifying that the training programme conducted by the petitioner was satisfactory or not. 5.3. By letter dated 14.09.2018, the Director of the Labour informed the Additional Chief Secretary, Labour and Employment Department that seven teams of officers were deployed to carry out inspection at the sites of ongoing health and safety training classes that were being conducted by the agencies empanelled by the respondent No.2. According to the petitioner, the inquiry report submitted by the team of officers indicated that the training classes being conducted by the petitioner - Trust were running regularly. Thereafter, by communication dated 27.09.2018, the Administrative Officer of the respondent No.2 informed the Project Managers of all the districts that the health and safety training scheme mooted by the respondent No.2 is ordered to be cancelled and that appropriate action be taken in this regard. 5.4. It is the case of the petitioner that by the time, the aforesaid order was received, the petitioner had already completed holding 50 training classes out of 70 training classes as per the work order Ishwar Gram Vikas Trust vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166016465/ 4 dated 07.05.2018 and the completion certificates were also issued by the concerned NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined Project Manager for the same. The petitioner, therefore, raised its invoices for the completed work, stating that an amount of Rs.33 lacs is due and payable to the petitioner by the respondent No.2 in respect of the 50 training classes conducted by the petitioner - Trust. It is the case of the petitioner that even after raising invoices, no payment was released by the respondent - Board. The petitioner, thereafter by letter dated 27.02.2019, requested the Member Secretary of the respondent No.2 to release the payment for the work carried out by it. 5.5 . Thereafter, a High Power Committee was constituted by the Labour and Employment Department to look into the matter of outstanding payment to be made to empanelled agencies for health and safety training conducted by them. It is the case of the petitioner that by communication dated 29.06.2021, the Deputy Secretary, Labour and Employment Department, informed the respondent No.2 that the report dated 10.06.2021 of the High Power Committee has been accepted and the State Government has granted approval for releasing payment within 7 days. The said communication requested for payments to be made to empanelled agencies after calculating the deductions to be made in the case of different empanelled agencies. It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner along with the other similarly situated agencies, who were issued work orders for different districts, made representations on 30.11.2021, 13.09.2022 and 17.04.2023 for release of the payment as per the decision communicated by letter dated 29.06.2021 to the respondent NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined No.2. 5.6. The petitioner replied to the notice on 09.10.2023 stating that as the notice does not indicate any deficiency in service, as alleged therein, the petitioner is not in a position to explain the same, more particularly, when the work completion certificate and opinion certificate have been issued by the Project Manager after completion of each training programme wherein, it is found that the training programme was conducted satisfactorily by the petitioner - Trust and the petitioner did not receive any payment of its outstanding dues. On the basis of the above opinion of the High Power Committee, the Deputy Secretary, Labor and Employment Department, addressed a communication dated 29.06.2021 to the respondent No.2 - Board that the report of High Power Committee has been accepted by the State Government and necessary action with regard to payment be taken. It appears that the additional affidavits are filed from time to time during the course of proceedings of this petition on behalf of the respondent No.2 as well as on behalf of the respondent No.1 to place on record the discrepancies found on scrutiny of the various files of the training classes conducted by the petitioner - Trust. It appears that the decision taken on 17.07.2023 for not releasing the security deposit of Rs.5 lacs was communicated by the respondent No.2 to the petitioner -Trust by letter dated 04.08.2023 and thereafter, the Show-Cause Notice was issued on 24.08.2023. 8.
texts.arguments: Learned Senior Advocate Mr.Shalin Mehta appearing with learned advocate Ms.Aditi S. Raol for the petitioner submitted that there is no Show Cause Notice issued for the work order dated 07.05.2018 by the respondents, alleging any irregularity in conducting of the training classes by the petitioner - Trust. The petitioner has never been informed about the irregularities, which are noted in the file notings which are made available for the perusal of the Court and it was, therefore, submitted that the respondents, in absence of any communication or Show Cause Notice, are required to release the outstanding payment of Rs.33 lacs to the petitioner - Trust. 9. In support of his submissions, reliance was placed on the decision of the Honorable Apex Court in the case of State of Orissa Vs. Laxmi Narayan Das (Dead) Thr. Lrs. and others reported in (2023)15 SCC 273 to submit that whether a party can rely on the notings wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that a party cannot rely on the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT Ishwar Gram Vikas Trust vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166016465/ 9 DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined notings in the government file without having communication of any order on the basis thereof. It was submitted that as no order was passed by the respondents and conveyed to the petitioner for not making the payment of the outstanding dues of Rs.33 lacs, the respondents are not justified in withholding the payment solely on the basis of the official notings in the file. 10. Per contra, learned Government Pleader Mr.G.H. Virk appearing with learned Assistant Government Pleader Ms.Dharitri Pancholi for the respondent No.1 referred to and relied upon the following decisions:- ( 1 ) Pimpri Chinchwad New Township Development Authority vs. Vishnudev Cooperative Housing Society and others, reported in (2018)8 SCC 215 to submit that the reliance placed by the petitioner on the communication dated 29.06.2021 between the two departments of the government could not have been referred to and relied upon as the decision referred therein was reviewed. It was pointed out that in the aforesaid case, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that mere noting in the official file of the Government while dealing with any matter pertaining to any person is essentially internal matter of the government and carries with it no legal sanctity and once the decision on such issue is taken and approved by the competent authority empowered by the government in that behalf, it is required to be communicated to the person concerned by the State Government. (2) Learned Government Pleader Mr.Virk thereafter referred to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Shanti Sports Club and another Vs. Union of India and others, reported in (2009)15 SCC 705 wherein, in the facts of the said case, the Hon'ble Apex Court after referring to the settled legal position, held as under:- "43. A noting recorded in the file is merely a noting simpliciter and nothing more. 44. In State of Punjab v. Sodhi Sukhdev Singh [AIR 1961 SC 493] this Court considered the question whether a provisional decision taken by the Council of Ministers to reinstate an employee could be made the basis for filing an action for issue of a mandamus for reinstatement and held: (AIR p. 512, para 42) "42. ... We are unable to understand this argument. Even if the Council of Ministers had provisionally decided to reinstate the respondent that would not prevent the Council from reconsidering the matter and coming to a contrary conclusion later on, until a final decision is reached by them and is communicated to the Rajpramukh in the form of advice and acted upon by him by issuing an order in that behalf to the respondent." 45. A somewhat similar question was considered by the Constitution Bench in Bachhittar Singh v. State of Punjab [AIR 1963 SC 395 : 1962 Supp (3) SCR 713] in the backdrop of the argument that once the Revenue Minister of PEPSU had recorded a note in the file that the punishment imposed on the respondent be reduced from dismissal to that NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined of reversion, the same could not be changed/reviewed/overruled by the Chief Minister. This Court proceeded on the assumption that the note recorded by the Revenue Minister of PEPSU in the file was an order, referred to the provisions of Article 166 of the Constitution and held: (AIR p. 398, paras 9-11) "9. ... Merely writing something on the file does not amount to an order. Before something amounts to an order of the State Government two things are necessary. Until Ishwar Gram Vikas Trust vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166016465/ 11 such an order is drawn up the State Government cannot, in our opinion, be regarded as bound by what was stated in the file. 10. The business of State is a complicated one and has necessarily to be conducted through the agency of a large number of officials and authorities. Therefore, until such advice is accepted by the Governor whatever the Minister or the Council of Ministers may say in regard to a particular matter does not become the action of the State until the advice of the Council of Ministers is accepted or deemed to be accepted by the Head of the State. Which of them can be regarded as the 'order' of the State Government? In this connection we may quote the following from the judgment of this Court in State of Punjab v. Sodhi Sukhdev Singh [AIR 1961 SC 493] : (AIR p. 512, para 42) '42. ... Mr Gopal Singh attempted to argue that before the final order was passed the Council of Ministers had decided to accept the respondent's representation and to reinstate him, and that, according to him, the respondent seeks to prove by calling the two original orders. Even if the Council of Ministers had provisionally decided to reinstate the respondent that would not prevent the Council from reconsidering the matter and coming to a contrary conclusion later on, until a final decision is reached by them and is communicated to the Rajpramukh in the form of advice and acted upon by him by issuing an order in that behalf to the respondent.' We are, therefore, of the opinion that the remarks or the order of the Revenue Minister, PEPSU are of no avail to the appellant." (3) Reliance was also placed on the decision of the coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of M/s.Global S.S. Construction Pvt. Ltd. vs. Chief General Manager, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined (Mechanical - I/C SEM) rendered in Special Civil Application No.11391 of Ishwar Gram Vikas Trust vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166016465/ 12 2020 and other allied matters on 30.07.2021 wherein, it is observed as under:- "36. It may, now, be pointed out that at the first stage of a contract, which requires the authorities concerned to formulate the terms and conditions subject to which the tenders would be invited or the contract would be allotted, many factors are taken into account. The decision as to what terms shall be included in the tender is really a policy decision, for, it is the authority issuing the notice inviting tender, which is the best judge to determine as to what terms and conditions would be required for successful completion of the work or the project concerned. However, when the invitation to tender is floated, the second stage, which consists of the process of selection of the person for awarding the contract, commences and this process comes to an end, when a decision either awarding the contract or cancelling the entire tender process is taken. The decision to award the contract is not open to judicial review; but the decision making process, which leads to the ultimate decision, is, according to the law laid down in TATA Cellular v. Union of India reported in (1994) 6 SCC 651, open to judicial review. In Raunaq International Ltd. v. IVR Construction Ltd and Ors. [AIR 1993 SC 393], the Apex Court has made it clear that though the decision to award a contract is not open to judicial review, the decision-making process, which leads to the ultimate decision, is, indeed, open to judicial review provided that there is an element of public interest involved in the case requiring a review by the Court of the administrative decision to allot the contract. 38. What may be further noted is that at the first and the second stage of the contracts, when the government or any of its instrumentalities sets up the terms and conditions of the contract or takes a NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined decision to allot the contract, it acts purely in its executive capacity and its action is, therefore, open to judicial review, though in a limited way, as indicated hereinabove. However, when the third stage is reached and a contract is entered into by the government or its instrumentality, on the one hand, and the contractor, on the other, the parties are no longer governed by Constitutional provisions, but by the terms of the contract. Hence, when a State, purporting to act within the field allotted to it under the terms and conditions of a contract, performs an act, the rights and obligations of the parties would be, ordinarily, governed by the law that governs the terms and conditions of the contract. The mere fact that one of the parties to such a contract is the State or its instrumentality will not make a contract amenable to writ jurisdiction. (See Radhakrishna Agarwal v. State of Bihar (supra))." (4) Learned Government Pleader Mr.Virk heavily relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Joshi Technologies International Inc. vs. Union of India and others, reported in (2015)7 SCC 728 wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under, when the writ petition is maintainable in cases where monetary claim is raised:- Ishwar Gram Vikas Trust vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166016465/ 13 "69. 69.1. The Court may not examine the issue unless the action has some public law character attached NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined to it. 69.2. Whenever a particular mode of settlement of dispute is provided in the contract, the High Court would refuse to exercise its discretion under Article 226 of the Constitution and relegate the party to the said mode of settlement, particularly when settlement of disputes is to be resorted to through the means of arbitration. 69.4. Money claims per se particularly arising out of contractual obligations are normally not to be entertained except in exceptional circumstances. approaching the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and invoking its extraordinary jurisdiction. 11. It was, therefore, submitted by learned Government Pleader Mr.Virk that considering the facts of the case emerging from the record, the petition may not be entertained as the petitioner was informed by the respondent No.2 - Board by communication dated 04.08.2023 that no payment is required to be made as per the notings at page 81 of the file notings referred in the said communication, followed by a Show-Cause Notice. It was, therefore, submitted that the case of the petitioner would squarely fall within the observation of the Hon'ble Apex Court as observed in para Nos.69.2 to 69.4, 70.6 and 70.8 in the case of Joshi Technologies International Inc. (supra). 12. It was further submitted by learned Government Pleader Mr.Vrik in a query raised by this Court, by filing an additional affidavit tendered during the course of hearing today wherein, it is averred as under:- "2. It is respectfully submitted that the Labour, Skill Development and Employment Department, Government of Gujarat, vide Government Resolution dated 21.05.2015, formulated a scheme for imparting training to construction workers (the "Scheme"). Looking to the discrepancies in imparting of the training as also NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined the implementation of the Scheme, the Scheme was cancelled on 19.09.2018. No payment has been made to any agency after September 2018, i.e. after cancelation of the Scheme. 3. None of the agencies, except the present Petitioner - Ishwar Gram Vikas Trust, have challenged the decision of the State Government as on date, either before this Hon'ble Court or before any other Hon'ble Court." 13. It was, therefore, submitted that no relief can be granted as prayed by the petitioner in this petition in the facts of the case and the petitioner can avail the alternative remedy in accordance with law. 14.

Even if the Council of Ministers had provisionally decided to reinstate the respondent that would not prevent the Council from reconsidering the matter and coming to a contrary conclusion later on, until a final decision is reached by them and is communicated to the Rajpramukh in the form of advice and acted upon by him by issuing an order in that behalf to the respondent.' We are, therefore, of the opinion that the remarks or the order of the Revenue Minister, PEPSU are of no avail to the appellant." (3) Reliance was also placed on the decision of the coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of M/s.Global S.S. Construction Pvt. Ltd. vs. Chief General Manager, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined (Mechanical - I/C SEM) rendered in Special Civil Application No.11391 of Ishwar Gram Vikas Trust vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166016465/ 12 2020 and other allied matters on 30.07.2021 wherein, it is observed as under:- "36. It may, now, be pointed out that at the first stage of a contract, which requires the authorities concerned to formulate the terms and conditions subject to which the tenders would be invited or the contract would be allotted, many factors are taken into account. The decision as to what terms shall be included in the tender is really a policy decision, for, it is the authority issuing the notice inviting tender, which is the best judge to determine as to what terms and conditions would be required for successful completion of the work or the project concerned. However, when the invitation to tender is floated, the second stage, which consists of the process of selection of the person for awarding the contract, commences and this process comes to an end, when a decision either awarding the contract or cancelling the entire tender process is taken. The decision to award the contract is not open to judicial review; but the decision making process, which leads to the ultimate decision, is, according to the law laid down in TATA Cellular v. Union of India reported in (1994) 6 SCC 651, open to judicial review. In Raunaq International Ltd. v. IVR Construction Ltd and Ors. [AIR 1993 SC 393], the Apex Court has made it clear that though the decision to award a contract is not open to judicial review, the decision-making process, which leads to the ultimate decision, is, indeed, open to judicial review provided that there is an element of public interest involved in the case requiring a review by the Court of the administrative decision to allot the contract. 38. What may be further noted is that at the first and the second stage of the contracts, when the government or any of its instrumentalities sets up the terms and conditions of the contract or takes a NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined decision to allot the contract, it acts purely in its executive capacity and its action is, therefore, open to judicial review, though in a limited way, as indicated hereinabove. However, when the third stage is reached and a contract is entered into by the government or its instrumentality, on the one hand, and the contractor, on the other, the parties are no longer governed by Constitutional provisions, but by the terms of the contract. Hence, when a State, purporting to act within the field allotted to it under the terms and conditions of a contract, performs an act, the rights and obligations of the parties would be, ordinarily, governed by the law that governs the terms and conditions of the contract. The mere fact that one of the parties to such a contract is the State or its instrumentality will not make a contract amenable to writ jurisdiction. (See Radhakrishna Agarwal v. State of Bihar (supra))." (4) Learned Government Pleader Mr.Virk heavily relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Joshi Technologies International Inc. vs. Union of India and others, reported in (2015)7 SCC 728 wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under, when the writ petition is maintainable in cases where monetary claim is raised:- Ishwar Gram Vikas Trust vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166016465/ 13 "69. 69.1. The Court may not examine the issue unless the action has some public law character attached NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/801/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined to it. 69.2. Whenever a particular mode of settlement of dispute is provided in the contract, the High Court would refuse to exercise its discretion under Article 226 of the Constitution and relegate the party to the said mode of settlement, particularly when settlement of disputes is to be resorted to through the means of arbitration. 69.4. Money claims per se particularly arising out of contractual obligations are normally not to be entertained except in exceptional circumstances. approaching the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and invoking its extraordinary jurisdiction.
